She was later recognized as a national martyr. [Source: Lyndon B. Johnson Presidential Library, Address to the Nation on Vietnam and Non-Candidacy, March 31, 1968]

<!-- id: EVT-2454 -->
*   **Nov. 1, 1968:** The US was forced to completely and unconditionally end the bombing and strafing of the North. The North defeated the first war of destruction, shooting down 3,234 US aircraft. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, History of Vietnamese Diplomacy (1945 - 2000), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2455 -->
*   **Nov. 27, 1968:** During a devastating B-52 carpet bombing by the US Air Force in Tan Chau, Chau Doc (now An Giang), Ut Tich and her third daughter, Lam Thi Tho, were severely injured and subsequently sacrificed their lives. [Source: Central Committee of the Fatherland Front, Alliance of National, Democratic and Peace Forces of Vietnam (1968 - 1977), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2008]

<!-- id: EVT-2456 -->
* **27/11/1968:** Martyr Nguyen Thi Ut (Ut Tich) (female guerrilla from Tam Ngai famous for her phrase "Fight even if only a rag of trousers is left") heroically sacrificed her life in a US B-52 bombing raid. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2457 -->
*   **Dec. 1968 - May 1969:** The US 9th Infantry Division conducted Operation Speedy Express, a ruthless counterinsurgency sweep across the Mekong Delta (primarily in Ben Tre/Kien Hoa). Utilizing overwhelming destructive firepower from artillery, helicopter gunships, and night airstrikes in free-fire zones, the operation resulted in the deaths of thousands of unarmed civilians (US forces reported 10,889 enemy dead but recovered only 748 weapons, later exposed by international journalists as a systematic civilian bloodbath). [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, The 1968 Tet General Offensive and Uprising, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1998]

<!-- id: EVT-2458 -->
* **26/12/1968:** Martyr Nguyen Van Giai (Warrant Officer, leader of cryptographic team B49, Intelligence Department of the South J22) heroically sacrificed his life countering an enemy sweep in Trang Bang, Tay Ninh. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2459 -->

### **Period of Defeating the Vietnamization of the War Strategy (1969 - 1972)**

*   **1969:** Georges Boudarel successfully defended his highly regarded doctoral thesis on the Vietnamese patriot Phan Boi Chau, officially becoming a university professor and a leading researcher on Vietnam. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2460 -->
*   **1969 - 1970:** The US military (primarily the 6th Psychological Operations Battalion, in coordination with the Air Force and Navy) launched **Operation Wandering Soul**, a psychological warfare campaign designed to exploit traditional Vietnamese cultural and spiritual beliefs that fallen soldiers who are not properly buried in their homeland are condemned to wander eternally as tormented spirits (*oan hồn*). US PSYOP units secretly produced **"Ghost Tape Number 10"**, blending eerie Buddhist funeral music, chants, temple bells, wailing laments of women and children, and the distorted voice of a 'fallen soldier' pleading with his comrades to surrender and return home before facing the same grim fate. The recordings were broadcast at night through high-powered loudspeakers mounted on UH-1 helicopters, Swift patrol boats, and backpack-mounted systems into remote jungles and Liberation Army tunnel networks. However, the campaign largely failed against the steadfast political resolve of Vietnamese soldiers, who quickly recognized the deception and concentrated heavy anti-aircraft and ground fire directly at the sound sources; the macabre broadcasts also backfired by terrifying allied South Vietnamese troops and local civilians. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, The 1968 Tet General Offensive and Uprising, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1998]

<!-- id: EVT-2461 -->
* **1969:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Lê Văn Thọ (Trung đội trưởng đặc công thuộc miền Đông Nam Bộ. Người tham gia trận đánh kho bom Tân Sơn Nhất năm 1952) passed away. [Source: Lyndon B. Johnson Presidential Library, Address Announcing Complete Cessation of Bombing of North Vietnam, Oct. 31, 1968]

<!-- id: EVT-2462 -->
* **1969:** Martyr Lý Văn Lâm (Trung đội phó du kích xã Lợi An. Trên đường đi dự Đại hội anh hùng, chiến sĩ thi đua miền Tây Nam Bộ lần 2 bị địch phục kích, ông và người em trai đã anh dũng chống trả và hy sinh) heroically sacrificed his/her life while carrying out combat missions defending the Fatherland. [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, History of the Air Force (1955 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2463 -->
* **1969:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Nguyễn Văn Hùng (Chiến sĩ đặc công thủy Quân khu Sài Gòn - Gia Định, Trung Đội Phó đội Công binh LLVT Sài Gòn - Gia Định, chiến sĩ nòng cốt trong nhiệm vụ đánh sập các cây cầu huyết mạch của miền Đông Nam Bộ bao gồm: Ông Nhiêu (Thủ Đức), Chẹt Sậy (Lương Quới),Giồng Quéo (Bình Chánh), Bến Lức (Long An),,) passed away. [Source: Richard Nixon Presidential Library; Institute of History, Hanoi, 2014]

<!-- id: EVT-2464 -->
* **1969:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Điểu Cải (Xã đội trưởng Đội du kích Đồng Nai) passed away. [Source: Military Region 7 High Command, History of the Saigon - Gia Dinh Commandos (1945 - 1975), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2010]

<!-- id: EVT-2465 -->
* **1969:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Nguyễn Thị Nê (Nữ du kích Củ Chi, huyện đội phó huyện đội Nam Củ Chi, người được thay mặt Đại hội Anh hùng chiến sĩ thi đua toàn Miền Nam lần thứ 2 (1967) viết thư gửi Bác Hồ để báo cáo tình hình hoạt động cách mạng của lực lượng du kích Củ Chi) passed away. [Source: Larry Berman, Perfect Spy: The Incredible Double Life of Pham Xuan An, HarperCollins, New York, 2007; General Department II - Ministry of National Defense]

<!-- id: EVT-2466 -->
*   **Jan. 19, 1969:** Raising the NLF Flag atop Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris (France): On the eve of the opening preparatory session of the four-party Paris Peace Talks on Vietnam, three young Swiss peace activists (Bernard Bachelard, Olivier Parriaux, and Noé Graff) secretly scaled the nearly 100-meter spire of Notre-Dame de Paris to hoist the Liberation flag (half red, half blue with a gold star) measuring nearly 10 square meters. The flag fluttered proudly over Paris all day, creating a worldwide media sensation and focusing international public opinion in solidarity with the just resistance of the Vietnamese people. [Source: Tuoi Tre Newspaper - Raising the Vietnamese flag atop Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris in 1969 deeply cherished, https://tuoitre.vn/hanh-dong-treo-co-viet-nam-o-nha-tho-duc-ba-paris-nam-1969-rat-dang-tran-trong-20241117185131924.htm]

<!-- id: EVT-2467 -->
*   **Jan. 20, 1969:** Richard Nixon was inaugurated as US President and implemented the "Vietnamization of the war" strategy and the "Nixon Doctrine." [Source: Vietnam Women's Union, Portraits of Heroic Vietnamese Women, Women's Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2468 -->
*   **Jan. 22 - Mar. 18, 1969:** **Operation Dewey Canyon:** The US 9th Marine Regiment conducted Operation Dewey Canyon, penetrating deep into the Da Krong valley and the Vietnam-Laos border region to sever the Ho Chi Minh Trail and destroy strategic logistics depots of the Liberation Army. Operating amidst rugged mountain terrain, Vietnamese forces stubbornly held their ground, relentlessly ambushing and besieging US firebases, downing numerous aircraft, and firmly safeguarding the strategic supply corridor to the southern battlefield. [Source: Vietnam Women's Union, Portraits of Heroic Vietnamese Women, Women's Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2469 -->
*   **Jan. 25, 1969:** The first plenary session of the four-party conference on Vietnam opened in Paris. [Source: Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, History of Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2470 -->
*   **Feb. 10, 1969:** While transporting classified documents from the base to the outskirts of Saigon, intelligence courier Nguyen Van Thuong (Hai Thuong) was ambushed and surrounded by enemy forces. He fought heroically until his last bullet and concealed the secret documents before being captured. Despite enduring brutal torture and having his legs amputated 6 times by his captors, he steadfastly refused to reveal any organizational secrets. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 60 Years of Special Traditional Vietnam - Cuba Relations (1960 - 2020), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2020]

<!-- id: EVT-2471 -->
*   **Feb. 25, 1969:** A US Navy SEAL team led by Bob Kerrey killed 21 civilians in Thanh Phong (Ben Tre). [Source: Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, History of Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2472 -->
*   **Mar. 1969:** Due to declining health from previous years of imprisonment, brutal torture by the enemy, and harsh operating conditions in the South, Dinh Thi Van was transferred back to Hanoi for medical treatment and assigned to intelligence training tasks. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2473 -->
*   **Mar. 2, 1969:** Thiều Văn Chỏi and 4 guerrillas ambushed enemy forces 300m from Vàm Bưng post (Ba Trinh, Kế Sách, Sóc Trăng), killing 7 enemy troops, capturing 3 rifles and a radio. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2474 -->
*   **Mar. 18, 1969 - May 26, 1970:** **Operation Menu:** US President Richard Nixon secretly authorized Operation Menu, directing the US Strategic Air Command to conduct over 3,800 clandestine B-52 carpet-bombing sorties dumping hundreds of thousands of tons of bombs along the Vietnam-Cambodia border corridor to destroy the Central Office for South Vietnam (COSVN) and Liberation Army supply hubs. This covert escalation failed to dislodge the Vietnamese resistance, as headquarters personnel and supply troops masterfully dispersed and shielded logistics lines, safeguarding both central leadership and reinforcements to the front lines. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of the Resistance War against the US (1954 - 1975), Vol. 4, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013; William Shawcross, Sideshow, 1979]

<!-- id: EVT-2475 -->
*   **Night of Mar. 26 - Morning of Mar. 27, 1969:** Thiều Văn Chỏi and a comrade dug fortifications on the riverbank in front of Vàm Bưng post, ambushing soldiers at dawn, killing 2 and wounding 1. [Source: Hau Giang Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Can Tho (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2476 -->
*   **Apr. 17, 1969:** US troops (Tiger Force) massacred 63 civilians in Khanh Giang and Truong Le hamlets (Nghia Hanh, Quang Ngai). [Source: Quang Ngai Provincial Party Committee, War Crimes of the US Military in Quang Ngai, Quang Ngai Publishing House, 2005; Michael Sallah & Mitch Weiss, Tiger Force, 2006]

<!-- id: EVT-2477 -->
*   **May 10 - 20, 1969:** As part of **Operation Apache Snow**, the Battle of A Bia Hill (Hill 937), widely known as the Battle of Hamburger Hill, took place in the A Shau and A Luoi valleys (Thua Thien). The US military mobilized forces equivalent to two divisions (led by the 101st Airborne Division) along with massive firepower (dropping 890 tons of explosive bombs, 115 tons of napalm, and firing over 19,000 artillery shells) to capture the peak defended by two battalions of the Liberation Army of South Vietnam. Utilizing the rugged terrain and solid fortifications, the Liberation Army fiercely held their positions, breaking dozens of US infantry assaults and inflicting heavy casualties on enemy forces. On the night of May 18, after achieving the objective of decimating enemy manpower, the Liberation Army strategically withdrew. US troops reached the peak on the afternoon of May 20, only to abandon it shortly thereafter. The extreme brutality and perceived futility of the battle caused a political shockwave in the US, accelerating the Nixon administration's shift away from "maximum pressure" towards the "Vietnamization" strategy and troop withdrawal. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of the 324th Division, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1992; Samuel Zaffiri, Hamburger Hill, Presidio Press, 1988]

<!-- id: EVT-2478 -->
*   **May 25, 1969:** President Nguyen Van Thieu established the National Social Democratic Front to consolidate political power in the South. [Source: Institute of History, History of Vietnam, Vol. 12 (1965 - 1975), Social Sciences Publishing House, Hanoi, 2014]

<!-- id: EVT-2479 -->
*   **Jun. 6-8, 1969:** The National Congress of Southern Delegates convened, establishing the **Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam** (PRG RSV). Architect **Huynh Tan Phat** was elected President, Lawyer **Nguyen Huu Tho** as Chairman of the Consultative Council, Lawyer **Truong Nhu Tang** as Minister of Justice, and **Nguyen Thi Binh** as Minister of Foreign Affairs. The congress also officially decreed the adoption of the NLF flag (half red, half blue with a five-pointed gold star) as the official National Flag of the Republic of South Vietnam. Madame Binh subsequently led the PRG RSV delegation at the Paris Peace Talks. [Source: https://nhandan.vn/vai-tro-va-nhung-dong-gop-to-lon-cua-chinh-phu-cach-mang-lam-thoi-cong-hoa-mien-nam-viet-nam-post756380.html]

<!-- id: EVT-2480 -->
*   **Jun. 18, 1969:** The State of Vietnam conferred the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces on 7 outstanding officers and soldiers of the Air Defense - Air Force Service and General Logistics Department: fighter ace Nguyễn Văn Cốc (credited with shooting down 11 US aircraft, the highest-scoring Vietnamese ace of the war; later Lieutenant General, Commander of the Air Force), fighter ace Nguyễn Hồng Nhị (credited with 8 air victories; later Major General, Deputy Commander and Chief of Staff of the Air Force), fighter ace Phạm Thanh Ngân (credited with 8 air victories; later Senior Lieutenant General, Director of the General Political Department), Nguyễn Huy Hồng (Sergeant, anti-aircraft artillery deputy platoon leader in Regiment 233, Division 361 Air Defense, defending Hanoi airspace), Bùi Xuân Chiến (Corporal, 100mm anti-aircraft gun squad leader in Regiment 240, Division 363 Air Defense, fought over 300 battles protecting Vinh city, Bến Thủy ferry, and Lai Vu bridge; later Major), Ngô Văn Tác (Lieutenant, vehicle commander and guidance officer in Surface-to-Air Missile Battalion 71, Regiment 285, Division 369), and Trần Công Nhỡn (Sergeant, truck driver platoon leader in Group 878, Waystation 16, Group 500 General Logistics Department, transporting supplies to the front). [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, History of the Vietnam People's Air Force (1955 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015; Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2481 -->
*   **Late July 1969:** Thiều Văn Chỏi and a comrade disguised in civil guard uniforms attacked Vàm Bưng and Mang Cá posts during an enemy feast, killing 5 and wounding 3 enemy soldiers, leading terrified enemy troops to build a shrine to "Ông Thần Chỏi" (God Chỏi) at Vàm Bưng post. [Source: Hau Giang Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Can Tho (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2482 -->
*   **Aug. 25, 1969:** President Ho Chi Minh sent a reply letter to US President Richard Nixon (responding to Nixon's letter dated July 15, 1969). This was his final diplomatic document before his passing just eight days later. In the letter, President Ho Chi Minh condemned the US war of aggression while affirming the goodwill and principled peace stance of the Vietnamese people: *"Our Vietnamese people are deeply devoted to peace, a real peace with independence and real freedom. They are determined to fight to the end, without fearing the sacrifices and difficulties in order to defend their country and their sacred national rights"*. He emphasized that to achieve an honorable peace, the United States must end its war of aggression, withdraw all US and allied troops from South Vietnam, and respect the right of the South Vietnamese population and the Vietnamese nation to self-determination without foreign interference. [Source: Ho Chi Minh Complete Works, Vol. 15 (1966 - 1969), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2011, pp. 601-604; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2483 -->
*   **Sep. 2, 1969:** At 9:47 AM on September 2, 1969, beloved President Ho Chi Minh passed away in Hanoi at the age of 79. The entire Party, military, and people of Vietnam turned grief into revolutionary action, resolutely determined to fulfill his sacred Testament. [Source: Party Central Committee, Special Communique on the Passing of President Ho Chi Minh; Nhan Dan Newspaper, Sept. 4, 1969]

![Historical Image](images/event_20260923_225153.webp)

*Source: Portrait of President Ho Chi Minh / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)*

<!-- id: EVT-2484 -->
*   **Sep. 4, 1969:** Following the death of President Ho Chi Minh, Fidel Castro and Cuban President Osvaldo Dorticós Torrado sent a condolence telegram highly praising his extraordinary revolutionary qualities and leadership. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 60 Years of Special Traditional Vietnam - Cuba Relations (1960 - 2020), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2020]

<!-- id: EVT-2485 -->
*   **Sep. 9, 1969:** At Khánh Hưng Pagoda (District 3, Saigon), Venerable Thích Pháp Lan - the abbot - secretly held a memorial service for President Ho Chi Minh at the very time the nation observed the state funeral at Ba Đình Square, attended by hundreds of intellectuals, students, and Buddhists. Amid strict bans by the Government of the Republic of Vietnam on any form of commemoration, he carefully designed a banner with couplets encoding the name "Chí Minh" and arranged the altar in the colors of the national flag, then burned the eulogy manuscript immediately after reading it to erase traces. As soon as the ceremony ended, the crowd took to the streets in protest but was dispersed by police. Subsequently, the Venerable was summoned to the Saigon Police General Headquarters for hours of questioning; with firm arguments - stressing that monks honor only patriots and that Ho Chi Minh was a patriot revered by the people - he compelled the authorities to release him the same day. The altar used in the memorial was later transferred to the Ho Chi Minh Museum for display. [Source: National Assembly Documents, Vol. 3 (1964 - 1971), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2008]

<!-- id: EVT-2486 -->
*   **Sep. 23, 1969:** The 3rd National Assembly elected Comrade Ton Duc Thang as President and Comrade Nguyen Luong Bang as Vice President of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam. [Source: National Assembly Documents, Vol. 3 (1964 - 1971), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2008]

<!-- id: EVT-2487 -->
*   **Oct. 4, 1969 (or Oct. 7, 1970 according to varying accounts):** **Battle of Suoi Soc (Sa Nghe).** Bui Van Thuyen and a militiaman named Chien were ambushed by two US battalions. After Chien was wounded, Thuyen fought alone from morning until 5:00 PM. Utilizing seven different types of captured and existing weapons, he continuously maneuvered and repelled multiple enemy assaults, reportedly eliminating hundreds of US troops (recorded as 360). In 1995, a US MIA delegation visiting the battlefield acknowledged the severe casualties and expressed astonishment upon learning they had faced a single Vietnamese fighter. [Source: Tom Wells, The War Within: America's Battle over Vietnam, University of California Press, 1994; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2488 -->
*   **Oct. 21, 1969:** The Prime Minister of the Republic of Vietnam signed **Decree No. 709-ND/NV** merging Dinh Hai Commune (Paracel Islands) into Hoa Long Commune, Hoa Vang District, Quang Nam Province. [Source: Richard Nixon Presidential Library, Address to the Nation on the War in Vietnam, Nov. 3, 1969]

<!-- id: EVT-2489 -->
*   **Nov. 17, 1969:** At 8:00 AM, Thiều Văn Chỏi single-handedly engaged an enemy platoon of 27 soldiers traversing Bưng Sấu field, killing 13 (including an officer), wounding 8, and capturing 2. This 1-versus-27 victory led enemy troops at Vàm Bưng post to erect a shrine to "Ông Thần Chỏi" in front of their base to pray for safety. [Source: Hau Giang Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Can Tho (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2490 -->
* **23/11/1969:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Nguyễn Văn Chánh (Trung tá, nguyên Phó chỉ huy trưởng động viên, Ban chỉ huy quân sự quận Thủ Đức. Tham gia trận đánh sân bay Biên Hòa, tiêu diệt nhiều sinh lực địch, phá hủy nhiều xe quân sự). [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2491 -->
*   **Dec. 20, 1969:** The State of Vietnam conferred and posthumously conferred the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces on outstanding officers and soldiers; conferring upon Mai Năng (Commander of Naval Water Sapper Group 126, who later directly commanded the naval assault liberating the Truong Sa / Spratly Islands in April 1975; later Major General, Commander of the Sapper Command); and posthumously conferring upon 4 martyrs: Bùi Ngọc Dương (combat engineer officer from Hanoi, heroically opened routes and sacrificed at Khe Sanh in 1968), Bế Văn Cắm (brave military combat medic from Cao Bang), Nguyễn Văn Bích (deputy commander of the bridge-demolition combat engineers of Sub-region 1 Saigon - Gia Dinh, who commanded the blowing up of Phu Cuong bridge in Binh Duong in 1968), and Nguyễn Văn Xơ (Deputy Political Commissar of Regiment 1, Division 9 Eastern Cochinchina, who commanded the assault on Quang Trung Training Center during the 1968 Tet Offensive). [Source: Sapper High Command, History of the Sapper Branch (1967 - 2007), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2492 -->
*   **December 20, 1969:** On the 9th anniversary of the founding of the National Liberation Front of South Vietnam, the Central Committee awarded the title Hero of the People's Armed Forces of Liberation to the Saigon - Gia Dinh Commando Forces, honoring the 16 golden words bestowed by President Ho Chi Minh: *"United in heart, resourceful and resilient, magnificently courageous, infinitely loyal"* (Đoàn kết một lòng, mưu trí kiên cường, anh dũng tuyệt vời, trung thành vô hạn). [Source: Military Region 7 High Command, History of the Saigon - Gia Dinh Commandos (1945 - 1975), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2010]

<!-- id: EVT-2493 -->
*   **Dec. 22, 1969:** On the 25th anniversary of the Vietnam People's Army, the State awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to exemplary figures: La Thị Tám (female Youth Volunteer hero at the Dong Loc T-junction bottleneck, who staunchly stood on a high vantage hill to count and locate 1,205 unexploded bombs for clearance), Kim Ngọc Quảng (truck driver in Company 1, Battalion 52, Waystation 14, Group 559, brave and resourceful driver known as the "Steed of Truong Son"), and Cao Lương Bằng (distinguished anti-aircraft and vehicle-killer combatant; later Major General in the Vietnam People's Army). [Source: 12th Army Corps, History of Truong Son Soldiers - Ho Chi Minh Trail (1959 - 2009), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2009]

<!-- id: EVT-2494 -->
* **24/12/1969:** Martyr Hoang Minh Dao (First Head of the Military Intelligence Department, Deputy Head of the Military Proselyting Commission of the Central Office for South Vietnam) heroically sacrificed his life in an ambush on the Vam Co Dong River. [Source: General Department II - Ministry of National Defense, History of Vietnam Defense Intelligence (1945 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015]

<!-- id: EVT-2495 -->
*   **1970 - 1974:** Saigon commando Tran Van Lai was arrested and brutally tortured twice by the enemy in Quang Ngai. Using a fake identity, he maintained absolute secrecy, protecting his mission and the revolutionary network. [Source: Military Region 7 High Command, History of the Saigon - Gia Dinh Commandos (1945 - 1975), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2010]

<!-- id: EVT-2496 -->
*   **1970s:** Cuba began granting numerous scholarships for Vietnamese students in medicine, agriculture, and science. Thousands of Vietnamese were trained in Cuba, with many becoming leading experts in Vietnam. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 60 Years of Special Traditional Vietnam - Cuba Relations (1960 - 2020), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2020]

<!-- id: EVT-2497 -->
*   **1970:** At the age of 17, Mai Ngoc Thoang (born 1953 in Thach Thanh, Thanh Hoa) volunteered to join the army. Weighing only 38kg, he secretly put bricks in his pockets to meet the 43kg weight requirement and was accepted into the 48th Regiment, 320B Division (now 390th Division, 12th Army Corps). [Source: 390th Division - 12th Corps, History of the 390th Division (1951 - 2011), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2011; People's Army Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2498 -->
* **1970:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Nguyễn Thị Hạnh (Trung đội trưởng du kích xã Mỹ Hạnh. Xây dựng và phát triển cơ sở, đội du kích và chỉ huy đội du kích đánh địch hàng trăm trận) passed away. [Source: Vietnam Women's Union, Portraits of Heroic Vietnamese Women, Women's Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2499 -->
* **1970:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Nguyễn Viết Phong (Xã đội trưởng xã Mỹ Thủy, huyện Hương Thủy, tham gia chiến đấu 45 trận, diệt 112 tên địch (có 34 tên Mỹ), phá hủy 10 xe quân sự, thu nhiều vũ khí, tài liệu,) passed away. [Source: Vietnam Women's Union, Portraits of Heroic Vietnamese Women, Women's Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2500 -->
* **1970:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Hồ Thị Kỷ (Nữ chiến sĩ Biệt động) passed away. [Source: Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, History of Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2501 -->
* **1970:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Huỳnh Minh Mương (Trung đội trưởng đơn vị bảo vệ Khu ủy Sài Gòn - Gia Định) passed away. [Source: Ben Tre Women's Union, The Long-Haired Army of Ben Tre in the Anti-US Resistance, Ben Tre Publishing House, 2000]

<!-- id: EVT-2502 -->
* **1970:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Lê Văn Dỵ (Tham gia Chiến dịch Điện Biên Phủ) passed away. [Source: Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, History of Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2503 -->
* **1970:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Nguyễn Văn Y (Quyền Trưởng ban An ninh Khu 8 (Trung Nam Bộ); Trưởng ty An ninh tỉnh Mỹ Tho (Tiền Giang), tỉnh Long Châu Sa) passed away. [Source: Larry Berman, Perfect Spy: The Incredible Double Life of Pham Xuan An, HarperCollins, New York, 2007; General Department II - Ministry of National Defense]

<!-- id: EVT-2504 -->
* **10/02/1970:** The State of Vietnam posthumously awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Nguyễn Văn Hùng (Chiến sĩ đặc công thủy Quân khu Sài Gòn - Gia Định, Trung Đội Phó đội Công binh LLVT Sài Gòn - Gia Định, chiến sĩ nòng cốt trong nhiệm vụ đánh sập các cây cầu huyết mạch của miền Đông Nam Bộ bao gồm: Ông Nhiêu (Thủ Đức), Chẹt Sậy (Lương Quới),Giồng Quéo (Bình Chánh), Bến Lức (Long An),,). [Source: Party Central Committee, Party Documents, Vol. 31, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2505 -->
*   **Feb. 10, 1970:** A prominent nighttime supernatural audio assault under Operation Wandering Soul was executed by US forces near Fire Support Base Chamberlain in Hau Nghia Province. Helicopters from the US 6th PSYOP Battalion circled over the jungle throughout the night, broadcasting "Ghost Tape Number 10" interlaced with recorded predatory tiger roars to terrify Liberation forces, but were met with fierce retaliatory ground and anti-aircraft fire from steadfast Vietnamese fighters. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of Vietnamese Volunteer Troops in Cambodia (1970 - 1975), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002]

<!-- id: EVT-2506 -->
*   **Mar. 6, 1970:** The Politburo issued a resolution on the campaign to improve the quality of Party members and recruit new members (Ho Chi Minh Class). [Source: Institute of History, History of Vietnam, Vol. 12 (1965 - 1975), Social Sciences Publishing House, Hanoi, 2014]

<!-- id: EVT-2507 -->
*   **Mar. 10, 1970:** Following the arrest of Saigon Student Union President Huynh Tan Mam, urban student movements across Southern Vietnam erupted in campus strikes, street demonstrations, hunger strikes, and the anti-war musical movement "Sing for My Compatriots," demanding university autonomy, release of student detainees, and an end to the war. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, History of Vietnamese Diplomacy (1945 - 2000), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002]

<!-- id: EVT-2508 -->
*   **Mar. 12, 1970:** Cambodian Prime Minister Lon Nol closed the Sihanoukville port to North Vietnamese shipments and issued a 72-hour ultimatum for all Vietnamese forces to leave Cambodia. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of the Resistance War against the US (1954 - 1975), Vol. 4, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2509 -->
*   **Mar. 18, 1970:** General Lon Nol, backed by the US, staged a coup to overthrow the neutral government of Prince Norodom Sihanouk in Cambodia, officially dragging Cambodia into the Second Indochina War. [Source: Thomas M. Grace, Kent State: Death and Dissent in the Long Sixties, University of Massachusetts Press, 2016; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2510 -->
*   **Mar. 23, 1970:** Following the Lon Nol coup, Cambodian Head of State Norodom Sihanouk issued a historic five-point proclamation from Beijing establishing the National United Front of Kampuchea (FUNK) and the Cambodian National People's Liberation Armed Forces, entering a close alliance with the peoples of Vietnam and Laos against US intervention and the Lon Nol regime. [Source: Hau Giang Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Can Tho (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2511 -->
*   **Apr. 1970:** **Battle of Bau Sen.** Bui Van Thuyen and two comrades (Son and Muoi Quang) formed a three-man cell to engage US troops. Severely wounded with his intestines exposed, Thuyen regained consciousness, pushed his intestines back in, bandaged himself, and managed to kill 3 advancing US soldiers with an M79 grenade launcher before using the weapon as a crutch to return to his unit. [Source: Tom Wells, The War Within: America's Battle over Vietnam, University of California Press, 1994; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2512 -->
*   **Apr. - May 1970:** The Lon Nol regime carried out a brutal massacre against Vietnamese residents in Cambodia (at locations such as Prasot, Takeo, Neak Loeang, and Svay Rieng). Hundreds to thousands of Vietnamese civilians were killed, their bodies thrown into the Mekong River and floating downstream to Dong Thap and An Giang in Vietnam. On May 13, the Saigon administration repatriated surviving Vietnamese but failed to strongly oppose the massacres. [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces in the Anti-US Resistance, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2513 -->
* **18/04/1970:** Female guerrilla Le Thi Hong Gam (deputy commune military commander in Cam Son, My Tho) bravely fought alone, downing an enemy helicopter before heroically sacrificing her life. [Source: Central Committee of Vietnam Women's Union, General Nguyen Thi Dinh, Women's Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005; Memoirs: No Name in the Roster]

<!-- id: EVT-2514 -->
*   **Apr. 24 - 25, 1970:** The Summit Conference of the Indochinese Peoples was held with delegations led by Premier Pham Van Dong (DRV), President Nguyen Huu Tho (Republic of South Vietnam), Prince Souphanouvong (Neo Lao Hak Sat), and Head of State Norodom Sihanouk (President of FUNK). The conference issued a joint declaration affirming unwavering solidarity and mutual determination to defeat US imperialist aggression across the entire Indochinese peninsula. [Source: Central Committee of Vietnam Women's Union; Nguyen Thi, The Mother with a Gun, Literature Publishing House, Hanoi, 1965]

<!-- id: EVT-2515 -->
*   **Apr. 30 - Jun. 30, 1970:** Over 100,000 US and Saigon troops launched the Cambodian Campaign, conducting 23 large-scale operations up to 80 kilometers deep into Cambodian territory to seek and destroy the COSVN headquarters. [Source: Ho Chi Minh City Women's Union, Life and Revolutionary Career of Comrade Le Thi Rieng, Ho Chi Minh City General Publishing House, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2516 -->
*   **Jun. 22, 1970:** Doctor and martyr Dang Thuy Tram courageously falls in Duc Pho (Quang Ngai) at age 28 while single-handedly fighting to defend her field clinic and wounded soldiers against a US raid. Her two diary notebooks ("Dang Thuy Tram's Diary") were subsequently saved by former U.S. military intelligence officer Frederic Whitehurst because *"it already has fire in it."* [Source: Hau Giang Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Can Tho (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2517 -->
*   **Jul. 2, 1970:** The Politburo issued Resolution No. 200-NQ/TW establishing the Central Council for Frontline Supply to mobilize manpower and resources for the battlefield. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of the 324th Division, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1992]

<!-- id: EVT-2518 -->
*   **July 2, 1970:** US congressional aides Tom Harkin and Don Luce, accompanied by international journalists, secretly discovered and photographed the concealed "Tiger Cages" at Con Son (Con Dao) Prison—where hundreds of patriotic Vietnamese political prisoners were subjected to inhumane torture (lime dusting, dirty water hosing, starvation, and shackling under US-funded advisory programs). The shocking exposé published in *Life* magazine laid bare these atrocities before global public opinion, igniting intense international anti-war protests demanding the closure of the cages and an end to the war. [Source: Don Luce, Hostages of War: Saigon's Political Prisoners, Indochina Mobile Education Project, 1973; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2519 -->
*   **Aug. 25, 1970:** Dinh Thi Van was awarded the noble title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces for her outstanding contributions to Vietnam's military intelligence. Tran Huu Bao also received this title for his exceptional combat achievements during the defense of Hill 595. [Source: General Department II - Ministry of National Defense, History of Vietnam Defense Intelligence (1945 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015]

<!-- id: EVT-2520 -->
* **25/08/1970:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Lê Hải (Đại úy, Đại đội trưởng Trung đoàn Không quân 923, phi công cấp Ace của Không quân nhân dân Việt Nam, bắn rơi 6 máy bay Mỹ. Sau này là Đại tá, Sư đoàn trưởng Sư đoàn Không quân 372). [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, History of the Vietnam People's Air Force (1955 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015]

<!-- id: EVT-2521 -->
* **25/08/1970:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Hoàng Văn Cón (from Cao Bằng). [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2522 -->
*   **Aug. 30, 1970:** The Women's Movement for the Right to Live (led by Lawyer Ngo Ba Thanh) along with the People's Committee for the Right to Live and labor unions staged major demonstrations in Saigon protesting tax increases, soaring inflation, demanding the withdrawal of US troops and the restoration of peace. [Source: Ho Chi Minh City Youth Union, History of Saigon - Gia Dinh Urban Movements (1954 - 1975), Tre Publishing House, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2523 -->
*   **Nov. 21, 1970:** **Operation Ivory Coast (Son Tay Raid):** The US military mobilized a joint special operations task group in a surprise airborne commando raid targeting the Son Tay POW camp (Son Tay town, Ha Tay) in an attempt to rescue captured American pilots held in North Vietnam. Demonstrating exceptional vigilance and strategic foresight, the army and people of North Vietnam had anticipated developments and proactively evacuated all American prisoners to another secure location well in advance. The US commando raid came up completely empty-handed and suffered an embarrassing tactical failure, while local antiaircraft and militia units fought back decisively, shooting down enemy aircraft. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of the Resistance War against the US (1954 - 1975), Vol. 4, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2524 -->
*   **1971:** Nguyen Thi Binh, Head of the negotiating delegation of the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam at the Paris Conference, visited Iraq and was welcomed with great honor by the Iraqi government and people. [Source: Nguyen Thi Binh, Family, Friends and Country (Memoir), Tri Thuc Publishing House, Hanoi, 2012]

<!-- id: EVT-2525 -->
*   **1971:** Georges Boudarel published the influential book "Tradition and Revolution in Vietnam" (Truyền thống và cách mạng ở Việt Nam). [Source: Georges Boudarel, Tradition et Revolution au Vietnam, Editions Anthropos, Paris, 1971]

<!-- id: EVT-2526 -->
* **1971:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Lê Văn Thế (Huyện đội trưởng huyện Củ Chi, tỉnh Gia Định) passed away. [Source: Military Region 7 High Command, History of Cu Chi District Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2000]

<!-- id: EVT-2527 -->
* **1971:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Chu Cẩm Phong (Công tác tại Ban Tuyên huấn Khu V, sau làm phóng viên thông tấn rồi chuyển sang làm việc tại Tiểu ban Văn nghệ Khu V. Nhà văn thuộc Hội Nhà văn Việt Nam) passed away. [Source: Vietnam Writers Association, War Diary of Writer Chu Cam Phong, Literature Publishing House, Hanoi, 2000]

<!-- id: EVT-2528 -->
* **1971:** Martyr Nguyen Van Thoat (soldier of the People's Armed Forces of Bac Kan province) heroically sacrificed his life while carrying out combat missions defending the Fatherland. [Source: Bac Kan Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Bac Kan (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2529 -->
*   **Feb. 8 - Mar. 24, 1971:** Route 9 - Southern Laos Campaign (Operation Lam Son 719). The Republic of Vietnam forces, heavily supported by 10,000 US troops, 1,200 aircraft, and heavy artillery, mobilized over 21,000 of their most elite troops (Airborne, Marines, Armor) to invade southern Laos to sever the Ho Chi Minh Trail at Tchepone. The Liberation Army of South Vietnam (with 60,000 troops) launched an unprecedented large-scale combined-arms counter-offensive. Highlighting the campaign was the decisive victory at Ban Dong (Mar. 12 - 20), where the Liberation Army shattered the ARVN 1st Airborne Brigade and two armored regiments. The campaign ended in a disastrous defeat for the Saigon army (suffering over 1,500 casualties and hundreds captured; losing 71 tanks, 163 armored vehicles, and having over 100 helicopters destroyed and 600 damaged). This victory marked a profound maturation of the Liberation Army, completely thwarted the goal of cutting the Truong Son trail, and dealt a fatal blow to the US "Vietnamization" strategy. [Source: Nhan Dan Newspaper - Route 9 - Southern Laos Campaign, https://special.nhandan.vn/chien-dich-duong-9-nam-lao/index.html]

<!-- id: EVT-2530 -->
*   **Apr. 20, 1971:** The Republic of Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest against Malaysia regarding territorial issues and took the opportunity to strongly reaffirm Vietnamese sovereignty over both the Paracel and Spratly archipelagos. [Source: Dr. Nguyen Nha, Vietnam's Territorial Sovereignty over the Paracel and Spratly Archipelagos, Tri Thuc Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2531 -->
* **13/05/1971:** Martyr Huynh Van Danh (Political Officer of the Tan Tru District Local Platoon, Long An) heroically sacrificed his life in a battle in Duc Hoa after participating in 134 battles. [Source: Long An Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Long An (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2532 -->
*   **June 16, 1971:** Nguyen Van Bach (son of Le Thi Tuyet from Tra Cu) died in battle at the Long Hiep front. [Source: The New York Times, June 13, 1971; The Pentagon Papers, Gravel Edition, Beacon Press, Boston, 1971]

<!-- id: EVT-2533 -->
*   **Jul. 1, 1971:** The Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam put forward a 7-point peace proposal at the Paris Conference. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2534 -->
*   **Jul. 11, 1971:** The Philippine President publicly announced that Republic of China (Taiwanese) troops had occupied and fortified Itu Aba Island (Ba Binh) in the Spratlys, although he did not express any specific Philippine claims to that particular island at the time. [Source: Dr. Nguyen Nha, Vietnam's Territorial Sovereignty over the Paracel and Spratly Archipelagos, Tri Thuc Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2535 -->
*   **Jul. 13, 1971:** Republic of Vietnam Foreign Minister Tran Van Lam reaffirmed Vietnam's sovereignty over the archipelagos at an international conference in Manila. [Source: Dr. Nguyen Nha, Vietnam's Territorial Sovereignty over the Paracel and Spratly Archipelagos, Tri Thuc Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2536 -->
*   **Jul. 16, 1971:** China's Xinhua News Agency strongly condemned the Philippine occupation of several islands in the Spratly archipelago and firmly reiterated China's claims over the region. [Source: Central Steering Committee for Natural Disaster Prevention; General Department of Meteorology and Hydrology, Hanoi]

<!-- id: EVT-2537 -->
*   **Sep. 20, 1971:** The State of Vietnam conferred and posthumously conferred the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces on outstanding cadres and fighters: conferring upon Phùng Quang Thanh (platoon leader in Company 9, Battalion 64, Regiment 64, Division 320, distinguished in the battle of Unnamed Hill during Operation Lam Son 719 / Route 9 - Southern Laos Campaign; later General, Politburo member, Minister of National Defense), Lê Mã Lương (prominent combatant famed for the quote "The most beautiful life is on the battlefront against the enemy", distinguished in the Route 9 - Southern Laos Campaign; later Major General, Director of the Vietnam Military History Museum), and Nguyễn Hữu Trí (Chief of Strategic Intelligence Section J22; later Colonel, former Deputy Commander of Ho Chi Minh City Military Command); and posthumously conferring upon female martyr Lê Thị Hồng Gấm (deputy guerrilla commander of Long Bình Điền commune, Mỹ Tho province, who single-handedly fought against enemy helicopters and infantry until her last breath). [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2538 -->
* **01/10/1971:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Hà Văn Vấn (Lái xe đường Trường Sơn). [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2539 -->
*   **Oct. 3, 1971:** Fierce demonstrations erupted in the streets of Saigon, Hue, Da Nang, and Quy Nhon protesting Nguyen Van Thieu's one-candidate "one-man race" presidential election; protesters burned US military vehicles and clashed with riot police. [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2540 -->
*   **Dec. 1971:** The 3rd Congress of the Vietnam Fatherland Front was held in Hanoi. [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2541 -->
*   **Dec. 20, 1971:** At the Congress of Heroes of the People's Armed Forces organized by the Mien Command, Bui Van Thuyen was officially awarded the title Hero of the People's Armed Forces by the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam for his exceptional bravery, creativity, and combat achievements. [Source: Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, History of Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2542 -->
* **1972:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Nguyễn Văn Ty (Đại đội trưởng bộ binh thuộc Trung đoàn 88, Đại đoàn 308, tham gia trận Điện Biên Phủ) passed away. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, Counter-offensive Campaign Route 9 - Southern Laos 1971, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1987]

<!-- id: EVT-2543 -->
* **1972:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Ngô Văn Cấn (Tiểu đoàn trưởng tiểu đoàn 9 bộ binh) passed away. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of the Resistance War against the US (1954 - 1975), Vol. 4, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2544 -->
* **1972:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Lê Thị Pha (Đại đội trưởng Đại đội nữ Pháo binh Y2 Đại Lào, Bảo Lộc (Tỉnh Lâm Đồng)) passed away. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, History of the Resistance War against the US (1954 - 1975), Vol. 4, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2545 -->
* **1972:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Nguyễn Thái Bình (Sinh viên trường Cao đẳng Nông lâm ở Sài Gòn dưới chế độ Việt Nam Cộng hòa. Tham gia nhiều phong trào phản chiến, trả tự do cho chiến sĩ cộng sản, đòi Mỹ rút quân và thay đổi chế độ ở miền Nam Việt Nam) passed away. [Source: Ho Chi Minh City Women's Union, Life and Revolutionary Career of Comrade Le Thi Rieng, Ho Chi Minh City General Publishing House, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2546 -->
* **1972:** Martyr Phan Văn Hân (Liệt sĩ, nguyên Thường vụ Khu ủy Sài Gòn - Gia Định, nguyên Bí thư Phân khu 2, Sài Gòn - Gia Định) heroically sacrificed his/her life while carrying out combat missions defending the Fatherland. [Source: Vietnam Women's Union, Portraits of Heroic Vietnamese Women, Women's Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2547 -->
*   **Feb. 14, 1972:** Female guerrilla liaison Nguyen Thi Tu (wife of Vinh Hung commune guerrilla commander Le Van Dong, known as Nam Dong) heroically sacrificed her life in Vinh Hung commune (Vinh Loi district, Bac Lieu province). Captured alongside her 10-month-old daughter and brutally tortured to force her to reveal the secret bunkers and resistance forces of her husband, she steadfastly refused to yield; before being executed, she courageously asked to breastfeed her baby daughter for the last time. Her unyielding sacrifice and sacred maternal love became the prototype for the renowned vọng cổ work "Giọt sữa cuối cùng" (The Last Drop of Milk) by playwright Trọng Nguyễn. [Source: Ben Tre Women's Union, The Long-Haired Army of Ben Tre in the Anti-US Resistance, Ben Tre Publishing House, 2000]

<!-- id: EVT-2548 -->
*   **Mar. 30, 1972:** The Liberation Army launched a massive artillery bombardment on Camp Carroll (Tan Lam base), a major military base in Quang Tri defended by the 56th Regiment under Pham Van Dinh. [Source: Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, History of Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2549 -->
*   **Mar. 30, 1972 - Jan. 31, 1973:** The 1972 Spring-Summer Strategic Offensive (Easter Offensive) erupted with three massive combined-arms strategic thrusts by the Liberation Army of South Vietnam across three main fronts: Tri-Thien, North Central Highlands, and Southeastern Vietnam (Nguyen Hue Campaign). The Liberation Army mobilized over 200,000 regular troops alongside hundreds of tanks and artillery pieces. In Tri-Thien, they shattered the Route 9 defense line, decimated the ARVN 3rd Division, and liberated Quang Tri province (May 2). In the Southeast, they captured Loc Ninh (Apr. 7), besieged An Loc, and blockaded Route 13. The offensive dealt a severe blow to the "Vietnamization" strategy, expanded the territory controlled by the Provisional Revolutionary Government by 10-20%, and created a major advantage at the Paris peace talks. [Source: Nhan Dan Newspaper - The 1972 Strategic Offensive, https://special.nhandan.vn/cuoc-tien-cong-chien-luoc-nam-1972/index.html]

<!-- id: EVT-2550 -->
*   **Apr. 2, 1972:** Facing annihilation and denied reinforcements or permission to retreat by his superiors, Lieutenant Colonel Pham Van Dinh surrendered Camp Carroll along with 1,500 soldiers of the 56th Regiment to the Liberation Army to save their lives. This unprecedented surrender severely shocked the Republic of Vietnam. Dinh was granted clemency, retaining his rank as a Lieutenant Colonel in the Vietnam People's Army and was assigned to enemy proselytizing tasks. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, Tri Thien - Hue Campaign and the 81 Days and Nights at Quang Tri Ancient Citadel in 1972, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002]

<!-- id: EVT-2551 -->
*   **Apr. 6, 1972:** The US conducted its second war of destruction against the North (Operation Linebacker I). [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2552 -->
*   **Apr. 17, 1972:** Female nurse Lê Thị Ngọc Tiến and medical assistant Lê Thị Lệ Chi heroically sacrificed their lives in Hòa Định commune (Chợ Gạo district, Tiền Giang province) to protect 18 severely wounded soldiers in a secret bunker. Captured and tortured but refusing to confess, when threatened with disembowelment by a US bayonet by a ruthless scout platoon leader at 5:00 AM, Tiến courageously defied him: *"If you dare, do it, don't threaten me, you will never get me to confess!"*. The enemy savagely disemboweled her and hung her body on a tamarind tree to terrorize the local resistance. [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2553 -->
*   **Apr. 23 - 24, 1972:** Battle of Dak To - Tan Canh (part of the North Central Highlands Campaign). Opening the campaign, the Liberation Army utilized T-54 tanks and AT-3 Sagger (B-72) anti-tank missiles for the first time in the Central Highlands. Employing highly effective diversionary tactics to trick the enemy into focusing defenses on the West, the Liberation Army launched a surprise deep-thrust attack from the East, rapidly annihilating the headquarters of the ARVN 22nd Division. Liberation Army tank number 377 single-handedly destroyed seven enemy M-41 tanks. The victory collapsed the enemy's strongest defense complex in the North Central Highlands, directly threatening Kon Tum city. [Source: Nhan Dan Newspaper - 50th Anniversary of Dak To - Tan Canh Victory, https://nhandan.vn/ky-niem-50-nam-chien-thang-dak-to-tan-canh-post694300.html]

<!-- id: EVT-2554 -->
*   **May 8, 1972:** US President Richard Nixon ordered Operation Pocket Money, laying over 3,000 magnetic mines and delayed-action bombs to blockade Haiphong harbor and strategic northern river mouths to sever maritime supply lines. Facing extremely dangerous mine-clearing missions with slim chances of survival, volunteer suicide squads (from Naval Engineer Team 8, the Maritime Safety Directorate, Tràng Cát Border Guard Post, and clearing detachments) held emotional "living funeral" ceremonies (*lễ truy điệu sống*) directly on the docks before setting out. During these solemn farewell rituals, soldiers wrote final letters, received wreaths, swore the oath *"Decide to die for the Fatherland to live"*, and courageously steered iron motorboats to detonate and defuse mines, successfully reopening the strategic shipping channels. [Source: Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, History of Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2555 -->
* **19/05/1972:** The State of Vietnam posthumously awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Hồ Thị Kỷ (Nữ chiến sĩ Biệt động). [Source: Ben Tre Women's Union, The Long-Haired Army of Ben Tre in the Anti-US Resistance, Ben Tre Publishing House, 2000]

<!-- id: EVT-2556 -->
* **19/05/1972:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Lê Xuân Tấu (Tư lệnh Binh chủng Tăng-Thiết Giáp). [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, The 1972 Strategic Offensive, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002]

<!-- id: EVT-2557 -->
*   **Jun. 1, 1972:** The Politburo issued Resolution No. 220-NQ/TW on shifting and promoting tasks in the North, transitioning the economy to wartime conditions to continue defeating the US aggressors. [Source: Binh Phuoc Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Binh Phuoc (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2558 -->
*   **Mid-1972:** At Vietnam's request, China sent personnel and equipment to assist in sweeping and dismantling naval mines and bombs dropped by the US in Vietnamese rivers and coastal waters. [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, History of the Air Force (1955 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2559 -->
*   **Jun. 28 - Sep. 16, 1972:** The Battle of Quang Tri Citadel took place over 81 days and nights of extreme intensity ("The Fiery Summer"). To gain leverage at the Paris Conference, the US and Saigon forces launched Operation Lam Son 72, mobilizing over 35,000 elite troops (Airborne, Marines) heavily supported by US air and naval power. Quang Tri town (less than 3 square kilometers) endured 120,000 tons of bombs (equivalent to 7 atomic bombs) and nearly 1.6 million artillery shells. Despite the apocalyptic firepower, the Liberation Army of South Vietnam (over 14,000 troops) fiercely held the trenches, repelling countless assaults and inflicting over 7,700 casualties on the enemy (the Marine Division alone suffered over 5,200 casualties). At midnight on Sep. 15, having fulfilled the strategic objective of maintaining negotiation leverage, the Liberation Army proactively withdrew across the Thach Han River. [Source: https://special.nhandan.vn/bao-ve-Thanh-co-Quang-Tri/index.html]

![Historical Image](images/event_20260923_130911.webp)

*Source: Victory smile at Quang Tri Citadel during the 81-day battle of 1972 (Photo: Doan Cong Tinh / People's Army Newspaper)*

<!-- id: EVT-2560 -->
*   **Jun. 28 - Sep. 16, 1972:** During the 81-day-and-night battle to defend Quang Tri Ancient Citadel, 14-year-old dispatch courier Nguyen Xuat Hien (2nd Battalion, 48th Regiment, 320B Division) courageously braved relentless bomb and artillery fire to deliver operational messages and guide units between frontline trenches. His indomitable spirit and cheerful resilience earned him the nickname "The Ancient Citadel's Oriole", becoming an iconic symbol of youthful bravery during the resistance war against the US. [Source: Military History Institute of Vietnam, The 1972 Strategic Offensive, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002]

<!-- id: EVT-2561 -->
*   **Jul. 13, 1972:** During the fierce battle to defend Quang Tri Ancient Citadel, after three comrades sacrificed their lives attempting to reconnect a severed communication line, Corporal Mai Ngoc Thoang and Quach Manh Nhac volunteered for the mission. While Nhac operated the crank generator on the bank, Thoang swam to the middle of the fast-flowing Thach Han River under intense enemy artillery fire. Finding the broken wires but lacking spare wire to tie them, he used his teeth to bite and hold the two ends together for 30 minutes, enduring severe electric shocks that caused him to repeatedly faint. His extraordinary act created a "living bridge" for communications, allowing General Vo Nguyen Giap to direct the 48th Regiment in repelling enemy attacks. [Source: 3rd Army Corps High Command, History of the Western Highlands Front - 3rd Army Corps (1964 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2562 -->
*   **Aug. 3, 1972:** During the 81-day-and-night defense of the Quang Tri Ancient Citadel, Senior Lieutenant Le Binh Chung (Deputy Political Commissar of the 3rd Battalion, Quang Tri Provincial Military Command) and his comrades tenaciously held their ground inside a command bunker under ferocious enemy bombardment. When surrounded and facing overwhelming firepower, the soldiers held firm to the last breath, courageously using their radio to call friendly artillery fire directly onto their own bunker coordinates to eliminate the assaulting enemy forces and heroically sacrifice for the nation. [Source: Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, History of Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2563 -->
*   **Sep. 27, 1972:** Thiều Văn Chỏi, Deputy Commander of Kế Sách District Military Command, fell into an ambush by an enemy civil guard platoon of Company 555 in ấp 7, Ba Trinh commune. Fighting single-handedly for 20 minutes, he heroically sacrificed his life. Between 1968 and 1972, he participated in 152 battles, eliminating hundreds of enemy troops. [Source: Nick Ut, The Terror of War, Associated Press; 1973 Pulitzer Prize for Spot News Photography]

<!-- id: EVT-2564 -->
*   **Oct. 8 - 20, 1972:** In secret talks in Paris, Special Adviser Lê Đức Thọ and U.S. National Security Advisor Henry Kissinger reached a breakthrough secret agreement on the draft "Agreement on Ending the War and Restoring Peace in Vietnam". The draft stipulated that the United States would end hostilities, completely withdraw all expeditionary forces and military advisers within 60 days, and respect Vietnam's fundamental national rights, while revolutionary armed forces remained in the South. Both sides privately agreed on a timetable to initial the agreement in Hanoi on October 22 and officially sign in Paris on October 31, 1972; President Richard Nixon cabled Premier Phạm Văn Đồng affirming the text was considered complete. [Source: Tom Wells, The War Within: America's Battle over Vietnam, University of California Press, 1994; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2565 -->
*   **Oct. 12, 1972:** First Secretary Le Duan sent a telegram to the Central Office for South Vietnam (COSVN) outlining urgent tasks upon the potential announcement of a peace agreement, emphasizing the need to seize control of rural areas, establish local revolutionary administrations, and combine political and military struggles to secure a favorable position ("land grab and flag planting"). [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2566 -->
*   **Oct. 26, 1972:** After the Nixon administration reneged on the agreed schedule—using objections from the Saigon government to delay signing and demanding 69 amendments—the Government of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam issued a public declaration disclosing the entire text of the secret agreement and agreed timetable, exposing the breach of faith to world public opinion. Put on the defensive just 12 days before the U.S. presidential election, National Security Advisor Henry Kissinger held an urgent White House press conference, delivering the famous declaration: *"Peace is at hand"* (*Hòa bình đang ở trong tầm tay*). The statement was essentially a political psychological maneuver designed to reassure American voters that the war was practically over, securing Richard Nixon's landslide reelection on November 7, while serving as a diplomatic stalling tactic for the US to prepare its massive December 1972 B-52 strategic bombing campaign in a bid to coerce concessions from Hanoi. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, The Diplomatic Front and the Paris Negotiations, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2567 -->
*   **Dec. 18 - 30, 1972:** The "12 Days and Nights of Hanoi" Campaign — The "Dien Bien Phu in the Air" Victory (defeating the US strategic air offensive Operation Linebacker II). Seeking to salvage the "Vietnamization" strategy and pressure the Democratic Republic of Vietnam into conceding core terms at the Paris negotiations, US President Richard Nixon launched a destructive strategic air campaign utilizing B-52 bombers against Hanoi, Hai Phong, and surrounding areas (destroying Kham Thien Street, Bach Mai Hospital, Yen Vien Station...). Under the direct leadership of the Central Military Commission and Commander-in-Chief Senior General Vo Nguyen Giap from General Headquarters (Building and Bunker D67 in the Thang Long Imperial Citadel), during 12 days and nights of resilient and ingenious combat, the armed forces and people of Hanoi alongside the Air Defense - Air Force Service created a historic miracle: shooting down 81 American aircraft, including 34 B-52 strategic bombers (16 falling on the spot) and 5 F-111 strike fighters, capturing numerous pilots. This crushing retaliation shattered US strategic air prestige, wrecked the plot to "bomb the North back to the Stone Age," forced the US to unilaterally halt bombing north of the 20th parallel on December 30 and sign the Paris Peace Accords (Jan. 27, 1973), withdrawing all expeditionary forces home. [Source: https://special.nhandan.vn/HaNoi_DienBienPhutrenkhong_12ngaydem/index.html]

![Historical Image](images/event_20260923_110125.webp)

*Source: TTXVN file photo*

<!-- id: EVT-2568 -->
*   **Dec. 22, 1972:** A screening of the film "Người chiến sĩ trẻ" was organized for Vietnamese soldiers heading to the fierce Son Na outpost on the Thua Thien Hue front. The image of the young hero Cù Chính Lan profoundly moved the troops, providing them with immense spiritual motivation before entering battle. [Source: Richard Nixon Presidential Library; Institute of History, Hanoi, 2014]

<!-- id: EVT-2569 -->
*   **Dec. 22, 1972:** During Operation Linebacker II, US strategic bombers carpet-bombed and devastated Bach Mai Hospital (the largest civilian hospital in North Vietnam), killing 28 doctors, nurses, hospital staff, and patients, and burying multiple treatment wings under rubble, sparking deep outrage among progressive global public opinion. [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, Hanoi - Dien Bien Phu in the Air (Dec. 1972), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002]

<!-- id: EVT-2570 -->
*   **Dec. 26, 1972:** On the night of Dec. 26, 1972, at the height of Operation Linebacker II, US B-52 bombers carpet-bombed and completely flattened the densely populated civilian street of Kham Thien (Hanoi) spanning over 1 km, killing 287 innocent civilians (mostly women, the elderly, and children), injuring 290 others, and destroying nearly 2,000 homes, temples, and schools. [Source: Hanoi City Party Committee, Kham Thien Bombing Memorial Relic; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

<!-- id: EVT-2571 -->
*   **Dec. 27, 1972:** During Operation Linebacker II ("Dien Bien Phu in the Air"), Captain Pham Tuan (5th Flight, 921st Air Regiment) piloted a MiG-21 interceptor taking off from Yen Bai forward airfield, skillfully evading American F-4 escort fighter screens to ambush a formation of B-52 strategic bombers over Moc Chau (Son La). He launched two air-to-air missiles, shooting down a B-52 on the spot and landing safely back at Yen Bai, becoming the first pilot in history to shoot down a B-52 in air-to-air combat. [Source: https://baochinhphu.vn/ky-tich-ban-roi-b52-bao-ve-binh-yen-bau-troi-ha-noi-102221212110615781.htm]

<!-- id: EVT-2572 -->
*   **Dec. 28, 1972:** During Operation Linebacker II ("Dien Bien Phu in the Air"), First Lieutenant pilot Vũ Xuân Thiều (9th Flight, 927th Air Regiment) took off in a MiG-21 from Cam Thuy forward airstrip (Thanh Hoa). Piercing heavy electronic jamming under ground radar guidance, he intercepted a formation of American B-52 bombers over Son La (Na San area). At extremely close range, after firing both air-to-air missiles without seeing the bomber immediately disintegrate, Vũ Xuân Thiều courageously throttled forward and rammed his MiG-21 directly into the B-52, sacrificing his life at age 27 to destroy the strategic bomber and scoring the second air-to-air B-52 kill for the Vietnam People's Air Force in the campaign. [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, History of the Vietnam People's Air Force (1955 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015]

<!-- id: EVT-2573 -->
*   **Dec. 30, 1972:** The US was forced to declare a halt to the bombing of the North from the 20th parallel northwards and agree to resume negotiations. [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, Hanoi - Dien Bien Phu in the Air (Dec. 1972), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2002]

<!-- id: EVT-2574 -->

### **1975 Spring General Offensive and Uprising, Complete Liberation of the South (1973 - Apr. 1975)**

*   **1973:** The Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam opened an Embassy in Iraq. The Iraqi government generously covered all operational expenses, including providing the headquarters, vehicles (including a new Citroen gifted by President Ahmed Hassan Al-Bakr), and daily living expenses to support Vietnam during the war. [Source: Nguyen Thi Binh, Family, Friends and Country, Tri Thuc Publishing House, Hanoi, 2012]

<!-- id: EVT-2575 -->
*   **1973:** During Fidel Castro's visit, Cuba donated five major socio-economic projects to Vietnam worth approximately $80 million, including the Thang Loi Hotel (Hanoi), Vietnam - Cuba Hospital (Dong Hoi), Xuan Mai road, Ba Vi cattle breeding farm, and Luong My poultry enterprise. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 60 Years of Special Traditional Vietnam - Cuba Relations (1960 - 2020), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2020]

<!-- id: EVT-2576 -->
* **1973:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Từ Văn Phước (Trung đội trưởng trinh sát đặc công huyện Lái Thiêu. Ba lần được tuyên dương "Dũng sĩ diệt Mỹ") passed away. [Source: Binh Duong Provincial Military Command, History of the People's Armed Forces of Binh Duong (1945 - 2005), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2577 -->
* **1973:** Hero of the People's Armed Forces Bùi Anh Tuấn (quê tại Vĩnh Phúc) passed away. [Source: Department of Propaganda and Training, Heroes of the People's Armed Forces, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1996]

<!-- id: EVT-2578 -->
* **11/01/1973:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Lê Thanh Đạo (Phi công cấp Ace của Không quân nhân dân Việt Nam. Bắn rơi 6 máy bay của Mỹ. Sau là Đại tá, Phó Ban Dân vận Trung ương). [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, History of the Vietnam People's Air Force (1955 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015]

<!-- id: EVT-2579 -->
* **11/01/1973:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Nguyễn Đức Soát (Phi công cấp Ace của Không quân nhân dân Việt Nam. Bắn rơi 6 máy bay của Mỹ. Sau là Trung tướng, Phó Tổng tham mưu trưởng Quân đội nhân dân Việt Nam). [Source: Air Defense - Air Force Service, History of the Vietnam People's Air Force (1955 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015]

<!-- id: EVT-2580 -->
*   **Jan. 15, 1973:** The US completely ended all acts of war against the North. [Source: Ministry of National Defense, History of the General Staff in the Anti-US Resistance (1954 - 1975), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1997]

<!-- id: EVT-2581 -->
*   **Jan. 27, 1973:** The **Paris Peace Accords** on ending the war and restoring peace in Vietnam were signed (negotiated by Special Advisor Le Duc Tho and signed by Foreign Ministers Nguyen Duy Trinh and Nguyen Thi Binh). The flag of the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam (the half-red, half-blue Liberation flag with a gold star) and the DRV red flag with a gold star flew proudly and on equal footing alongside the flags of the great powers at the Kléber International Conference Center in Paris, affirming the international legitimacy and political standing of the southern revolution. The US committed to respecting Vietnam's independence, sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity. [Source: https://nhandan.vn/hiep-dinh-paris-1973-buoc-ngoat-trong-cuoc-khang-chien-cuu-nuoc-cua-dan-toc-post736150.html]

![Historical Image](images/event_20260923_104849.webp)

*Source: File photo / Tien Phong Newspaper*

<!-- id: EVT-2582 -->
*   **Feb. - Apr. 1973:** The Truong Son Troops Command and Vietnamese Security Escort forces successfully mounted a special mission escorting Cambodian Head of State Norodom Sihanouk and Princess Monique along the Ho Chi Minh Trail (via Lao Bao and Route 9 in Lower Laos) to safely visit Cambodia's liberated zone, refuting hostile propaganda and consolidating Indochinese solidarity. [Source: 12th Army Corps, History of Truong Son Soldiers - Ho Chi Minh Trail (1959 - 2009), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2009]

<!-- id: EVT-2583 -->
*   **Feb. 15, 1973:** Following the signing of the Paris Peace Accords, steadfast intelligence operative Nguyen Van Thuong (Hai Thuong) was returned to freedom at Loc Ninh (Binh Phuoc) after 4 years of imprisonment and brutal torture across various enemy detention centers. [Source: General Department II - Ministry of National Defense, The Man Whose Legs Were Severed Six Times - Major Nguyen Van Thuong, People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2584 -->
* **27/03/1973:** Martyr Le Van Tach (First Lieutenant, Political Officer of the 89th Intelligence Liaison Battalion, 22nd Group) heroically sacrificed his life on the Southeastern intelligence liaison line. [Source: General Department II - Ministry of National Defense, History of Vietnam Defense Intelligence (1945 - 2015), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2015]

<!-- id: EVT-2585 -->
*   **Mar. 29, 1973:** The last US combat unit withdrew from South Vietnam in accordance with the Paris Peace Accords. On the same day, broadcaster Trịnh Thị Ngọ ("Hanoi Hannah") aired her final broadcast directed at American troops on the Voice of Vietnam, concluding eight consecutive years (1965–1973) of the historic psychological warfare program "A Small Talk to American GIs". [Source: https://cand.vn/nho-nhung-ngay-thang-ba-lich-su-post295070.html]

<!-- id: EVT-2586 -->
*   **Apr. 1973:** The Saigon-based magazine *Đối Diện* published a memoir titled "Trong niềm hòa hợp" (In the Spirit of Harmony) authored by Pham Van Dinh, advocating for national reconciliation, love, and the elimination of hatred to resolve the Vietnam War. [Source: Institute of History, History of Vietnam, Vol. 12, Social Sciences Publishing House, Hanoi, 2014]

<!-- id: EVT-2587 -->
*   **May 1973:** The Politburo issued a Resolution on the struggle to implement the Paris Agreement, combining political, military, and diplomatic means to force the adversary to comply. [Source: Party Central Committee, Party Documents, Vol. 34, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2588 -->
* **01/05/1973:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Phạm Thanh Quyết (Chiến sĩ thuộc Trung đội 4, Đại đội 91, Tiểu đoàn 35, Binh chủng Đặc công). [Source: Sapper High Command, History of the Sapper Branch (1967 - 2007), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2589 -->
*   **Jul. 1973:** The 21st Conference of the Party Central Committee (3rd tenure) affirmed that the path of the southern revolution was still the path of violence, preparing for the final stage of the resistance war. [Source: Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, History of Quang Tri Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2590 -->
*   **July 7, 1973:** Dr. Vu Dinh Tung, former Minister of War Invalids, founding President of the Vietnam Red Cross Society, Director of the Central Health Department, and a prominent patriotic Catholic intellectual who dedicated his life to the national liberation cause and Vietnamese medicine, passed away in Hanoi at the age of 78. [Source: Case-Church Amendment, US Public Law 93-52, 87 Stat. 130, July 1, 1973; Institute of History, Hanoi, 2014]

<!-- id: EVT-2591 -->
* **03/09/1973:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Phạm Tuân (Chiến sĩ Đại đội 5, Trung đoàn 921, Sư đoàn 371. Người đầu tiên bắn rơi máy bay B-52 của Mỹ và trở về an toàn (27/12/1972). Người đầu tiên của Việt Nam và châu Á bay vào vũ trụ (1980). Sau là Trung tướng, Chủ nhiệm Tổng cục Công nghiệp Quốc phòng). [Source: Party Central Committee, Party Documents, Vol. 34, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2004]

<!-- id: EVT-2592 -->
*   **Sep. 6, 1973:** The Republic of Vietnam Minister of Interior signed **Decree No. 420-BNV/HCDP/26** annexing Spratly Island, Amboyna Cay, Itu Aba, Northeast Cay, Southwest Cay, Loaita, Thitu, Namyit, Sin Cowe, and adjacent features to Phuoc Hai Commune, Dat Do District, Phuoc Tuy Province. [Source: Decree No. 1018-ND-ND of July 9, 1973 by RVN Ministry of the Interior; White Paper on Vietnam's Sovereignty, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 1982]

<!-- id: EVT-2593 -->
*   **Sep. 12 - 15, 1973:** Fidel Castro made his first historic visit to Vietnam. He delivered a speech in Hanoi on September 12 emphasizing the heroic struggle of the Vietnamese people. On September 15, he visited the liberated zone of Quang Tri, standing at Hill 241, becoming the first and only foreign head of state to visit South Vietnam's liberated zone before 1975. During this trip, he directed his personal medical team to save a 17-year-old female militia member, Nguyen Thi Huong, who was injured by unexploded ordnance at the Ben Hai River. [Source: Dr. Nguyen Nha, Vietnam's Territorial Sovereignty over the Paracel and Spratly Archipelagos, Tri Thuc Publishing House, Hanoi, 2013]

<!-- id: EVT-2594 -->
*   **Sep. 21, 1973:** In Paris, representatives of the Government of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam and the Government of Japan signed a Joint Communiqué formally establishing diplomatic relations at the ambassadorial level. This milestone opened a new chapter in bilateral relations following the 1973 Paris Peace Accords and initiated complex diplomatic negotiations to address unresolved issues stemming from World War II. [Source: Presidential Decree No. 420-NV of Sept. 6, 1973 by Republic of Vietnam; White Paper on Vietnam's Sovereignty, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 1982]

<!-- id: EVT-2595 -->
*   **Oct. 1973:** Special Advisor Le Duc Tho declined the 1973 Nobel Peace Prize (awarded jointly with Henry Kissinger), affirming that real peace had not yet been restored in Vietnam while US forces continued intervention. [Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 60 Years of Special Traditional Vietnam - Cuba Relations (1960 - 2020), National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2020; Nhan Dan Newspaper]

![Historical Image](images/event_20260924_111742.webp)

*Source: Advisor Le Duc Tho at Orly Airport, Paris, 1972 / Associated Press (Wikimedia Commons, Public domain)*

<!-- id: EVT-2596 -->
*   **Oct. 6, 1973:** By this date, the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam had been recognized by and established diplomatic relations with 34 countries. [Source: Ho Chi Minh City Women's Union, Life and Revolutionary Career of Comrade Le Thi Rieng, Ho Chi Minh City General Publishing House, 2007]

<!-- id: EVT-2597 -->
*   **Oct. 13, 1973:** The Party Central Committee issued Resolution No. 227-NQ/TW (21st Plenum), defining the basic task of the Southern revolution in the new stage as continuing the national people's democratic revolution and using revolutionary violence to seize power. [Source: Ministry of National Defense, History of the General Staff in the Anti-US Resistance (1954 - 1975), People's Army Publishing House, Hanoi, 1997]

<!-- id: EVT-2598 -->
*   **Dec. 3, 1973:** Eight commandos from Team 5 (Group 10 Rung Sac) attacked the Shell fuel depot at Nha Be, destroying 35 million gallons of gasoline and oil, and many facilities of the enemy. [Source: War Powers Resolution, US Public Law 93-148, 87 Stat. 555, Nov. 7, 1973; Institute of History, Hanoi, 2014]

<!-- id: EVT-2599 -->
* **03/12/1973:** Martyr Nguyen Cong Bao (Sergeant Major, suicide squad platoon leader, 5th Company, 10th Rung Sac Commando Group) heroically sacrificed his life after raiding and destroying the Nha Be Fuel Depot. [Source: Larry Berman, Perfect Spy: The Incredible Double Life of Pham Xuan An, HarperCollins, New York, 2007; General Department II - Ministry of National Defense]

<!-- id: EVT-2600 -->
*   **Dec. 9, 1973:** In Saigon, the Faculty of Letters of the University of Saigon in conjunction with the National Cultural Council convened a major scholarly symposium commemorating the 75th anniversary of Trương Vĩnh Ký's passing. The seminar gathered prominent southern intellectuals, reflecting lively academic debates contrasting his pioneering role in romanized culture and journalism against questions regarding his political engagement during early French colonial rule. [Source: Vietnam Women's Union, Portraits of Heroic Vietnamese Women, Women's Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2601 -->
* **20/12/1973:** The National Liberation Front / Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Nguyễn Minh Thắng (Trung Đội phó trinh sát Tiểu đoàn Quyết Thắng, Quân khu Sài Gòn - Gia Định). [Source: Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, History of Thua Thien Hue Provincial Party Committee, Vol. 2, National Political Publishing House, Hanoi, 2005]

<!-- id: EVT-2602 -->
* **31/12/1973:** The State of Vietnam awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces to Triệu Xuân Tâng (Chiến sĩ Binh đoàn 28, Quân khu Tây Bắc tham gia quân tình nguyện tại Lào).
